open_points.subject: first-release import and production rollout
open_points.text: Registry goes into production with it, and with it makes the one import (R0-79, R0-98).
open_points.question: Must the one import succeed before production serves consumers, or may Registry serve an empty or partially prepared production store while the import is pending or refused?
options: Gate production traffic on a successful import
Start production first and import while it is serving
Keep production available after a refused import and let the owner retry
Treat a refused import as a failed rollout
open_points.default_guess: Gate production traffic on the successful atomic import; a refused import fails the rollout until corrected and retried.

witness.initial: The first release is admitted, production's store is empty, and the VPS export contains a project already named by Client Portal.
events: Client Portal requests the known project before the import has succeeded.
The owner then performs an import that either succeeds or is refused for a conflict.
outcomes: Production is not exposed until import succeeds, so Portal never observes the project as missing.
Production serves before import succeeds, so Portal observes not_found or remains without the project after a refused import.
witness.observer: The owner and Client Portal users

open_points.subject: first-release protection for room names and aliases
open_points.text: until then the rule binds the owner, and the agent through the governance's instructions to it.
open_points.question: Who puts the governance rule into the agent's effective instructions before the second release, through what concrete mechanism, how is its presence verified, and what happens if it is absent?
options: The owner installs and verifies a system instruction before production use
Cabinet Kernel injects the governance instruction into every agent session
Agent room and alias writes remain unavailable until the manifest description is updated
The first release relies only on an unenforced governance rule
open_points.default_guess: Make the owner install and verify the instruction as a production-readiness step, and disable agent writes if it is missing.

witness.initial: The first release is running; its manifest description has not yet received the second-release change.
events: Kernel starts an agent session without any separately installed governance instruction.
The agent adds a room named "bathroom for the wheelchair".
Registry accepts the name and returns it to the agent and its AI provider.
outcomes: A careful implementation injects the governance instruction, so the agent is told not to write the name.
A careful implementation treats the abstract rule as sufficient without an injection mechanism, so the agent receives no such instruction and may write the name.
witness.observer: The owner, the customer whose health information is exposed, and the AI provider

open_points.subject: first-release visibility of refused attempts
open_points.text: until the second release the owner meets their purposes by hand — the yearly review from the governance's schedule, and signs of an attempt from the infrastructure.
open_points.question: How can infrastructure provide signs of the attempts that R0-97 says appear to it as ordinary HTTPS and only Registry can distinguish, while the first release explicitly has no Registry counters or trace?
options: Accept that the owner has no visibility of Registry-only attempts until the second release
Add a first-release Registry signal or trace
Change the infrastructure so it can classify these refusals
Limit the interim claim to attempt types the infrastructure can actually observe
open_points.default_guess: Limit the interim claim to infrastructure-visible events and state that Registry-only refused attempts are not visible until the second release.

witness.initial: The first release is running without R0-97 counters, behind the owner's VPN and WireGuard channel.
events: A caller sends an authenticated-looking HTTPS service request with a token Registry does not know.
The infrastructure forwards it as ordinary HTTPS.
Registry refuses it and keeps no trace.
outcomes: R0-97 yields no owner-visible sign because only Registry could classify the refusal.
R0-100 promises that the owner obtains a sign of the attempt from infrastructure.
witness.observer: The owner investigating a suspected breach
